title: Successor Desk Note: A Sale or Retention Already Under Way and the Successor Runway in Maturity and Due-and-Payable Cases
content:
**Rule.** For a Maturity and Due-and-Payable Cases case on a Cedarline Summit loan reclassified on the death of the last surviving borrower:

- Where the case already carries a received extension request supported by a listing agreement or a financing commitment, and the most recent accepted intent declaration on the case declares a sale or a retention of the property, 7 calendar days are taken off the runway length.
- Where that declaration declares a sale or a retention but the case carries no such request, 3 calendar days are taken off.
- Otherwise nothing is taken off.

**Most recent declaration.** Among accepted intent declarations made on the same day, the most recent is the one recorded later by its recorded date and time.

**"Received" request.** A received request is an extension request on the case whose status is received, meaning it is still awaiting a decision.

## Truth table

| Received extension request backed by a listing agreement or financing commitment | Most recent accepted intent declaration | Days taken off the runway length |
|---|---|---|
| yes | sell the property, or retain the property | 7 |
| no | sell the property, or retain the property | 3 |
| yes | deed in lieu, or no accepted declaration | 0 |
| no | deed in lieu, or no accepted declaration | 0 |

## Hypothetical illustration

A case shows an accepted declaration to sell, recorded in the morning, and an accepted declaration of deed in lieu, recorded later the same afternoon. The afternoon declaration is the most recent, so nothing is taken off, whatever extension requests are on the case.
